ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: Appeared in all 6/6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the strongest consensus signal of the batch. Apple's September 9 'Surprise and Shine' event is a hard-dated binary catalyst featuring the first-ever foldable iPhone Ultra alongside the iPhone 18 line, and the debut of new CEO John Ternus; Morgan Stanley estimates the foldable alone drives ~$14B in Q4 revenue. Stock has weakened into the event (Sept 5–6), creating a pre-event dislocation, but elevated implied volatility makes a defined-risk call debit spread far superior to outright stock given post-event IV crush risk.
ideas.catalyst: September 9, 2026 — Apple 'Surprise and Shine' event; foldable iPhone Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro/Max reveal; new CEO debut
ideas.edge: Morgan Stanley Buy/$360 PT implies ~9% upside from ~$330; foldable ASP materially above Pro Max with MS estimating $14B incremental Q4 revenue; wide analyst target dispersion ($303–$400) confirms binary setup favoring defined-risk options over stock
ideas.bull_case: A successful foldable launch resets the iPhone upgrade cycle narrative and could push AAPL toward the $360 MS target; new CEO Ternus delivering a polished event debut would further restore sentiment after the recent dip.
ideas.bear_case: KeyBanc flags a likely 'sell-the-news' reaction; if foldable supply is constrained or pricing disappoints, IV crush post-event could punish outright option buyers and the stock could retrace further on macro rate headwinds.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ ADR)

ideas.edge: 14-analyst consensus Strong Buy with $247.31 average target vs. ~$177 last price = ~39.7% implied upside; stock retesting $178.43 August high — a volume breakout above that level is a technically clean swing trigger with institutional support

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: Appeared in 4/6 runs as the preferred macro event vehicle straddling the September 11 CPI and September 16 FOMC twin catalysts. The Nasdaq-100's heavy concentration in AAPL, MSFT, and NVDA makes QQQ the highest-beta expression of both the Apple event (Sept 9) and the rate binary — a cool CPI could flip hike odds from ~58% back toward 30–35%, sparking a sharp tech relief rally as seen after Waller's comments (+1.4% single-session), while a hot CPI or hawkish dot plot could compress multiples 3–5%. A straddle or call spread with Sep 12 or Sep 19 expiry defines risk on both outcomes.
ideas.catalyst: August CPI print September 11, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET; FOMC rate decision + dot plot September 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM ET
ideas.edge: ~58% market-implied hike probability creates near-binary odds; a dovish CPI surprise could replicate the +1.4% single-session Nasdaq rally seen after prior Waller comments; Nasdaq QTD slightly negative, amplifying asymmetry on a dovish outcome
ideas.bull_case: A softer-than-expected CPI flips rate odds materially, triggering a Nasdaq short-squeeze combined with Apple event euphoria — QQQ call spread captures leveraged upside with defined cost.
ideas.bear_case: A hot CPI followed by a hawkish hike with revised dot plot could reprice QQQ 3–5% lower; high IV into the events means straddle theta decay is punishing if the index grinds sideways.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: Appeared in 3/6 runs with consistent medium conviction. NVDA has reset to a forward P/E of ~23.9x — only a 14% premium to the S&P 500 — despite posting 128% EPS growth last quarter, 62% net margins, and sell-side projections of 58% revenue CAGR through FY2029. The stock is up only ~2% YTD vs. S&P +7%, creating a relative underperformance gap that makes it a compelling swing entry on any FOMC-driven dip, though the September 16 rate decision coin-flip (~58% hike odds) is a near-term overhang that warrants a defined-risk structure.
ideas.catalyst: FOMC rate decision September 16, 2026 (binary macro overhang); confirmed Q3 FY2027 earnings November 17, 2026 AMC
ideas.edge: Forward P/E of 23.9x is only a 14% premium to the S&P 500 for a company with 58% projected revenue CAGR FY26–FY29 and 62% net margins; EPS +128% YoY last quarter; stock up only ~2% YTD vs. S&P +7% — a meaningful relative underperformance gap for the dominant AI infrastructure name
ideas.bull_case: A dovish CPI or Fed hold on September 16 re-rates high-growth tech multiples upward; NVDA's near-market valuation combined with dominant HBM/AI positioning makes it the highest-quality rebound candidate in the sector.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish hike with upward dot plot revisions would be the first rate increase of this cycle and could disproportionately compress NVDA's still-premium multiple; November 17 earnings are 10+ weeks away, limiting near-term fundamental catalysts.

ideas.catalyst: Ongoing US-Iran Strait of Hormuz hostilities (open-ended escalation risk); FOMC September 16, 2026 — energy benefits from higher-for-longer inflation outcome
ideas.edge: Energy is #1 S&P sector Q3 2026 (+21% QTD); integrated majors at 8–12% FCF yields vs. market average; XLE up 30%+ YTD yet supported by $90+ oil; options available for defined-risk call spreads to limit downside on sudden de-escalation

ideas.bear_case: A diplomatic resolution or ceasefire in the Iran conflict could collapse the geopolitical risk premium rapidly; a Fed-driven demand destruction signal could simultaneously pressure oil prices and unwind the YTD energy trade.
